items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.one_liner: An actively exploited Check Point vulnerability has been added to the KEV, requiring immediate attention for SOC and incident response teams.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-123039, an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability affecting multiple Check Point products, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog. The addition is based on evidence of active exploitation, making it a priority for remediation under Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04. Federal agencies are required to prioritize patching this vulnerability on publicly exposed assets, as it can grant total control of the system post-exploitation. CISA also encourages private organizations to adopt this risk-based management approach to mitigate potential breaches.
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-123039 is now confirmed to be under active exploitation, and organizations using Check Point products must prioritize its remediation.

claims.text: CISA added CVE-2026-123039 to the KEV Catalog due to active exploitation.

items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Active exploitation of critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities targets internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks management interfaces.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has evaluated its product portfolio regarding two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which affect PAN-OS software on PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls, and Panorama. CVE-2026-109618 allows RCE via uninitialized request memory after out-of-memory errors handled by longjmp(), while CVE-2026-109619 leaves global memory pointing to freed memory regions. Active exploitation has been observed against management interfaces exposed to the internet, prompting the vendor to assign a critical CVSS score of 9.2 and recommend restricting management access or deploying virtual patches.
key_facts: CVE-2026-109618: CVSS 9.2, remote code execution via OOM longjmp
CVE-2026-109619: remote code execution via global memory pointing to freed regions
items.bottom_line: Administrators must restrict external access to firewall management interfaces immediately to mitigate actively exploited critical PHP vulnerabilities.

claims.text: CVE-2026-109618 involves a remote code execution vulnerability where handling out-of-memory errors via longjmp() leaves request memory uninitialized due to improper control flow management, allowing attackers to reliably achieve RCE using out-of-memory (OOM) triggers.

claims.text: Active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet.

items.title: CVE-2026-114713: UnrealIRCd UnrealIRCd Improper Neutralization of Delimiters Vulnerability
items.one_liner: CISA added an UnrealIRCd delimiter neutralization flaw to its KEV catalog, requiring urgent patching.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-114713, an improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability in UnrealIRCd, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw allows network users on linked servers to inject server-to-server commands executed with server authority. Federal agencies are mandated to apply vendor mitigations or discontinue use of the product by November 16, 2026.
items.bottom_line: UnrealIRCd servers are vulnerable to unauthenticated server command injection via improper delimiter handling.

items.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
items.one_liner: A new Windows zero-day exploits CLFS and Windows Defender to grant local attackers full System privileges.
items.summary: Researcher Nightmare Eclipse has disclosed a Windows zero-day vulnerability named SignDrop, which allows local users to escalate privileges to System rights. The exploit leverages the Common Log File System (CLFS) and forces Windows Defender to process a crafted log container. This technique effectively turns a security-focused process into a tool for privilege escalation.
key_facts: Affected component: Common Log File System (CLFS)
Impact: Local privilege escalation to System
items.bottom_line: Attackers can now abuse Windows Defender's own update mechanisms to achieve local privilege escalation.

claims.text: On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows.
claims.support_span: On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows.

items.title: Check Point gateways hacked via PHP2Shell to deploy VMware ESXi wiper
items.one_liner: Check Point security gateways are being exploited via PHP2Shell to wipe VMware ESXi hosts.
items.summary: Check Point Security Gateway instances have been targeted by attackers exploiting a PHP2Shell vulnerability to deploy data-wiping malware directly onto underlying VMware ESXi hosts. The campaign leverages remote execution vectors to compromise perimeter security hardware and inflict catastrophic virtual machine data loss. Organizations utilizing Check Point gateways must immediately apply vendor patches and audit systems for indicators of compromise.
items.bottom_line: Attackers are chaining PHP2Shell exploits on Check Point gateways to execute destructive VMware ESXi hypervisor wipers.

claims.text: Vulnerable Check Point Security Gateway instances have been targeted in PHP2Shell attacks that deployed data-wiping malware on VMware ESXi hosts.

items.title: Meta Fined €805 Million in Italy Over Facebook’s Default Photo Gallery Access
items.one_liner: Meta faces a massive fine in Italy for violating privacy regulations by accessing Android photo galleries without informed, granular user consent.
items.summary: Italy’s data protection authority, the Garante, has fined Meta €805 million for unauthorized access to Android users' photo galleries. The investigation found that the Facebook app accessed photos, videos, and metadata without explicit user consent, using a single, overly broad permission. The feature, which suggested gallery content for posting, was enabled by default and lacked clear disclosure. Meta has 60 days to comply with the order to obtain specific consent and clarify the feature's data usage.
items.bottom_line: Regulators are increasingly penalizing 'default-on' data access features that bypass granular user consent requirements.

claims.text: Italy’s data protection authority, the Garante, has fined Meta Platforms Ireland Limited €805 million.
claims.support_span: The Italian Data Protection Authority (Garante) has fined Meta Platforms Ireland Limited €805 million.

claims.support_span: Through the Facebook app for Android devices, the company accessed photos, videos, and related metadata stored on Italian users’ smartphones without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them.

items.title: Businessman loses ₹1.45 crore in alleged cyber fraud
items.one_liner: Deepfake-based financial fraud is causing significant monetary losses in India, targeting individuals with sophisticated AI-generated impersonations of public figures.
items.summary: A businessman from Kozhikode, Kerala, lost ₹1.45 crore to a cyber fraud scheme involving an AI-generated deepfake video of Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. The fraudsters used the video to promote a fraudulent high-return investment scheme, convincing the victim to transfer funds in 30 separate installments. Local police have registered a case and are investigating the incident, which follows a similar scam in Vadakara. Authorities have issued warnings regarding unverified financial schemes and deepfake advertisements on social media.
items.bottom_line: The use of high-quality deepfakes to impersonate government officials is a growing threat to financial security in India.

items.title: New N-central Exploits Work Against Patched Servers, Enable Root RCE and Windows SYSTEM Access
items.one_liner: New N-central vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated root RCE and Windows SYSTEM access via exposed legacy APIs.
items.summary: Security researchers have disclosed new vulnerabilities codenamed 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell affecting on-premise versions of N-able N-central running version 2026.4.1 HF2. The flaws enable unauthenticated remote code execution with root privileges and weaponize managed Windows agents as SYSTEM, specifically targeting servers with the non-default Legacy API enabled. Threat intelligence firms observed active exploitation probes attempting to chain CVE-2026-90436 with these new exploits within hours of publication.
items.bottom_line: Threat actors are actively probing N-central servers with legacy APIs enabled to chain RCE and root privilege escalation flaws.

items.title: FBI flash alert says Artex tool automating cyberattacks at ‘machine speed’
items.one_liner: Monitor the proliferation of the Artex AI exploitation framework and its use by threat actors in automated, machine-speed cyberattacks.
items.summary: An FBI flash alert warns that the open-source AI platform Artex is being actively exploited by cybercriminals and nation-states to automate multi-stage cyberattacks at machine speed. Released on GitHub in August by Chinese cybersecurity engineer Li Puhua, the framework converts large language models into hacking tools that handle reconnaissance through data exfiltration in under three hours. Despite the repository's removal, the tool continues to spread via forks and commercial variants, with researchers noting widespread usage by Chinese-nexus groups targeting critical infrastructure and financial institutions across multiple countries. The platform integrates various AI models, with DeepSeek models being particularly prevalent due to a lack of observable guardrails.
key_facts: Exposed instances: over 1,600 publicly exposed Artex console instances
items.bottom_line: The FBI has issued an alert regarding the open-source Artex platform, which is being widely used by threat actors to automate complex cyber intrusions from reconnaissance to data exfiltration using large language models.

items.title: ZDI-26-964: (Pwn2Own) Philips Hue Bridge HomeKit Accessory Protocol chacha20_decrypt Integer Underflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated RCE in Philips Hue Bridge allows nearby attackers to compromise the smart home hub.
items.summary: A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability has been disclosed in the Philips Hue Bridge, affecting the HomeKit Accessory Protocol (HAP) service. The flaw, discovered during Pwn2Own, is an integer underflow that occurs when the service parses pairing requests on TCP port 8080. Network-adjacent attackers can exploit this without authentication to execute arbitrary code on the device. A fix has been released in Bridge v2 software version 1975170000.
items.bottom_line: Users of Philips Hue Bridge must update to version 1975170000 immediately to mitigate an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability.

items.title: CVE-2026-0324 GlobalProtect App: Incorrect Privilege Management Vulnerability in OPSWAT MetaDefender Endpoint Security SDK on Windows (Severity: MEDIUM)
items.one_liner: This vulnerability is critical for your Windows endpoint security work as it provides a direct path for local privilege escalation via a common security tool.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has disclosed a medium-severity privilege escalation vulnerability in the GlobalProtect app for Windows. The flaw originates in the integrated OPSWAT MetaDefender Endpoint Security SDK and allows a locally authenticated non-administrative user to gain NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges. No special configuration is required for exposure, though Palo Alto Networks reports no known exploitation in the wild. The issue is resolved by updating to GlobalProtect versions that include MetaDefender SDK 4.3.4822 or later.
items.bottom_line: Local users on Windows systems running vulnerable GlobalProtect versions can escalate to full SYSTEM privileges due to a flaw in the third-party OPSWAT SDK.

items.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
items.one_liner: SilentAir exploited hacked telecom equipment in Asia using SS7 and Diameter signaling to intercept 2FA codes.
items.summary: A state-level spying group named SilentAir hacked equipment inside mobile operators across at least six Asian countries to intercept SMS 2FA codes and calls, primarily targeting individuals in Taiwan. Security firm Enea discovered that the attackers exploited SS7 and Diameter signaling protocols by sending fraudulent UpdateLocation messages via compromised IPX network infrastructure. The operations occurred in intermittent bursts since early 2025 and targeted various government and political VIPs. Enea has notified the affected operators, though it remains unclear whether the compromised equipment has been cleaned.
items.bottom_line: Compromised operator equipment allows state-level actors to silently intercept mobile calls and 2FA codes via SS7 and Diameter signaling.

items.one_liner: ZDI-26-984 in TrendAI Vision One Security Agent allows local attackers to achieve SYSTEM execution via a heap buffer overflow.
items.summary: A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability, designated ZDI-26-984, affects the TMBMServer component of the TrendAI Vision One Security Agent. items.title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Vulnerabilities, Including a Code Execution Flaw That Reportedly Dates Back Two Decades…
items.one_liner: A critical 20-year-old type confusion vulnerability in PostgreSQL requires immediate patching across all supported versions.
items.summary: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has released security updates for versions 14 through 18, addressing 52 vulnerabilities. The most critical is CVE-2026-6460, a type confusion bug with a CVSS score of 8.8 that allows authenticated users with object-creation privileges to execute arbitrary code as the database OS user. This flaw reportedly dates back two decades and affects all currently supported major versions. Additionally, PostgreSQL 14 has reached its end-of-life, meaning this release is its final update.
items.bottom_line: If you have users with object-creation privileges, you are exposed to a high-severity RCE vulnerability that requires an immediate binary update.

items.title: CVE-2026-129349 - Apache Shiro: DefaultLdapRealm accepts any password when authentication caching is enabled
items.one_liner: Apache Shiro's LDAP authentication caching flaw allows attackers to bypass password checks after an initial successful login.
items.summary: A vulnerability in Apache Shiro (CVE-2026-129349) allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication when caching is enabled in DefaultLdapRealm. Once a user successfully logs in, subsequent authentication attempts for that user skip the LDAP bind process and accept any password due to the default installation of AllowAllCredentialsMatcher. The issue affects all versions through 3.0.0. Users are advised to upgrade to version 3.0.1 or disable authentication caching to mitigate the risk.
items.bottom_line: If your application uses Apache Shiro with LDAP authentication caching enabled, it is currently vulnerable to trivial credential bypass.

items.title: Barracuda Networks is your new best friend (Barracuda Email Security Gateway Pre-Auth Remote Root RCE CVE-2026-116606 / CVE-2026-111560)
items.one_liner: Critical pre-auth RCE in Barracuda ESG appliances requires immediate patching to prevent full network compromise via the mail gateway.
items.summary: Security researchers have detailed a critical exploit chain in Barracuda Email Security Gateway (ESG) involving CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560. The first vulnerability is a pre-authentication authorization bypass that allows arbitrary configuration restoration, while the second is an OS command injection flaw. When combined, these allow an unauthenticated attacker to achieve remote root code execution (RCE) on the appliance. Barracuda has released version 9.4.0.029 to address these issues, which also affect other products like the Load Balancer ADC and WAF.
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can gain root RCE on Barracuda ESG appliances by chaining a pre-auth bypass with a command injection vulnerability.

items.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
items.one_liner: Cisco issued an informational advisory regarding the emergency distrust of eMudhra intermediate CAs due to weak key generation.
items.summary: Between October 17 and October 20, 2026, a critical security compromise was uncovered involving Certificate Authorities managed by eMudhra. A security researcher demonstrated that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken due to an error in their Key Generation Ceremony in April 2025, enabling anyone to brute-force acquire the private keys within seconds. Cisco issued an informational security advisory regarding the emergency distrust of these eMudhra root and intermediate certificate authorities across products. Similar advisories have been published by Cisco Talos and Splunk.

items.title: Cisco BroadWorks Out-of-Band Blind XML External Entity Injection Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical XML external entity injection vulnerability in Cisco BroadWorks allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to exfiltrate sensitive configuration files.
items.summary: Cisco BroadWorks contains a critical vulnerability in its Open Client Interface (OCI) XML Parser that allows unauthenticated, remote attackers to read sensitive configuration files. The flaw stems from improper parsing where external entity resolution is enabled by default. Attackers can exploit this by sending a crafted XML message to the OCI-P service, potentially gaining access to sensitive filesystem data. Cisco has released software updates to address this issue, and there are no available workarounds.

items.one_liner: CISA has mandated the patching of a root-level privilege escalation vulnerability in Check Point security products.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-123039 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, highlighting an incorrect permission assignment in multiple Check Point products. The vulnerability exists in the Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon, which listens on a world-writable local socket without authentication. items.one_liner: Cyrus SASL's SRP implementation allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication by manipulating public values.
items.summary: Cyrus SASL (versions through 2.1.28) contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in its SRP server mechanism. The flaw occurs because the srp_server_mech_step2 function fails to reject client public values that are multiples of N, allowing unauthenticated attackers to force a zero shared secret. This enables attackers to authenticate as any user without a password and potentially obtain session keys.
items.bottom_line: Systems using Cyrus SASL for SRP authentication are vulnerable to complete authentication bypass by unauthenticated network clients.

items.title: Open WebUI: the Windows installer mints the master key from the install second — CVE-2025-15603 was rejected; here is the measurement
items.one_liner: Open WebUI's Windows installer uses a weak, predictable seed for its master secret key, allowing full session token forgery.
items.summary: The Windows installer for Open WebUI generates a master secret key using a linear congruential generator seeded only by the installation time in seconds. This flaw allows an attacker to recover the master key in approximately 2.1 seconds, enabling the forgery of administrator session tokens. Despite being reported as CVE-2025-15603, the vendor disputed the finding and rejected the CVE, claiming no action was required. New research confirms the vulnerability persists across all 178 release tags, with most lacking even basic per-account session stamps.
key_facts: Vulnerability: Predictable master secret key generation
items.bottom_line: Administrators should assume all Open WebUI installations on Windows are compromised and rotate all secrets immediately.

items.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
items.one_liner: LLMON is an XML-like markup language designed to defeat prompt injection and replace brittle JSON parsing in LLMs.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced LLMON (LLM Object Notation), an LLM-native markup language designed to replace JSON for causal language models by using reserved special-token delimiters for explicit structure and data binding. By wrapping semantic components in tags and mapping unique identifiers to instructions, the format prevents indirect prompt injections and stops models from pulling unrelated context into answers. IBM has released two experimental preview models based on Granite 4.1 (3B and 8B parameters) trained natively on LLMON, alongside a GitHub toolkit for conversions and workflows.
items.bottom_line: Adopting LLMON and its supporting Granite models eliminates indirect prompt injection risks by explicitly binding instructions to data payloads.

items.one_liner: UnrealIRCd CVE-2026-114713 is actively exploited in the wild, requiring immediate patching of IRC servers before federal compliance deadlines.
items.summary: CISA has added a high-severity command injection vulnerability in UnrealIRCd to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after active attacks were observed in the wild. Tracked as CVE-2026-114713 with a CVSS score of 8.6, the flaw stems from the labeled-response module failing to escape IRCv3 label message tags when echoing replies, allowing multi-server network users to execute arbitrary commands with server authority. Project maintainer Bram Matthys released hotfix version 6.2.7.1 on November 7, 2026, urging administrators to update immediately or apply a spamfilter workaround. Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies have until November 16, 2026, to apply the patches under BOD 26-04.
items.bottom_line: UnrealIRCd version 6.2.7.1 or a spamfilter workaround must be deployed immediately to counter active remote command injection exploitation of CVE-2026-114713.

items.one_liner: Midnight Blue found six unauthenticated root RCE zero-days in Danfoss refrigeration controllers that attackers are weaponizing to spoil food and cause fires.
items.summary: Midnight Blue researcher Carlo Meijer discovered six pre-authentication remote code execution zero-day vulnerabilities in the Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controller during a manual firmware review of versions up to 5.3.2. Asset owners are urged to restrict controller management access to VPNs, private APNs, or strict IP allowlists rather than relying solely on patches.

items.title: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question
items.one_liner: A new benchmark, XYBench, evaluates an AI's ability to identify and correct user misconceptions rather than blindly following flawed requests.
items.summary: XYBench is a new benchmark designed to test how well AI assistants handle the 'XY problem,' where users ask for help with a misguided approach (Y) rather than their actual goal (X). The benchmark consists of over 8,000 questions across programming and everyday tasks, measuring whether models can identify implicit misconceptions and redirect users toward effective solutions. Evaluation of top models like GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 showed that they often focus on the user's mistaken approach rather than addressing the underlying problem.
key_facts: Award: Best Resource Paper at EMNLP 2026
items.bottom_line: Current LLMs struggle to recognize the 'XY problem,' often providing answers to the wrong question instead of diagnosing the user's actual underlying need.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.summary: Amazon Web Services has open-sourced the Universal Agent Evaluation Framework (UAEF), an evaluation system that scores AI agents the same way regardless of which framework built them. items.one_liner: A memcached command injection vulnerability in older Perl HTTP::Session versions allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands via crafted session IDs.
items.summary: A vulnerability (CVE-2011-10042) has been identified in HTTP::Session versions before 0.43 for Perl, allowing memcached command injection. The flaw exists because the session ID from a client cookie is passed to memcached as a cache key without proper filtering. An attacker can inject CR and LF characters into the session ID to terminate the cache command early and execute arbitrary memcached commands. Users are advised to upgrade to version 0.43 or later, or migrate to an alternative like Plack::Middleware::Session.
items.bottom_line: Applications using outdated versions of HTTP::Session are at risk of memcached command injection and should be updated or migrated immediately.

items.summary: Last Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) grounded all flights in the United States for nearly four hours due to a reported equipment failure. The routers used to communicate with aeroplanes in mid-flight had suddenly stopped working, and pilots were no longer able to speak on their usual frequencies.
